definition: A regularization technique that randomly disables a fraction of neurons during training to prevent overfitting.
details: By forcing the network to not rely on any single neuron, dropout encourages redundancy and more robust feature representations, improving generalization to unseen data.
story: Imagine teaching a friend to shoot a basketball. They miss, and you walk them backwards through the shot — elbow, wrist, release — to find what needs fixing. Boil it down and it is this: A regularization technique that randomly disables a fraction of neurons during training to prevent overfitting. Here is why it matters: By forcing the network to not rely on any single neuron, dropout encourages redundancy and more robust feature representations, improving generalization to unseen data. It is learning from every miss instead of repeating the same mistake. That steady, miss-by-miss improvement is Dropout.

citation.title: Dropout: A Simple Way to Prevent Neural Networks from Overfitting
